result.summary:
REVIEWER narrow re-gate on WF03-ISS0210-20260821, rework commit 6954304. PASS on both acceptance criteria.

AC1 -- Re-opened handoffs/WF03-ISS0200-20260821/step-final-git-merge.json directly (not from memory). It confirms: every push in that run was a plain fast-forward (git_evidence.push_status: 'pushed, fast-forward only ... no force-push and no --force-with-lease issued at any point'); the branch was rebased twice as origin/main moved twice; rather than push into a rejection, the agent reset to its published tip and merged origin/main in, then proved the resulting tree byte-identical to the discarded rebase's tree. No non-fast-forward rejection was ever observed in that run -- it was a real structural risk that was anticipated (ORCH's mid-step correction authorizing --force-with-lease) and then avoided by the reset+merge route, never hit.

Against that source, git show 6954304 -- docs/agents/protocols/GIT_MERGE.md docs/issues/ISS-0210.yaml shows both flagged sentences reworded correctly:
  - GIT_MERGE.md step 6's parenthetical now reads: '...anticipated exactly this deadlock after its branch was rebased twice, and its dispatch was corrected mid-step to authorize --force-with-lease on its own branch -- but the agent avoided ever needing the push by resetting to its published tip and merging origin/main in instead, so the rejection itself was never actually observed there.'
  - ISS-0210.yaml's resolution_note now reads: '...whose dispatch was corrected mid-step to anticipate exactly this deadlock -- though the agent avoided ever needing the push by resetting to its published tip and merging origin/main in instead, so the rejection itself was never actually observed there.'
Both now correctly state anticipated-and-avoided (never observed), and both correctly attribute the avoidance to the reset-and-merge-origin/main route rather than to a force-push. Neither oversells the structural argument (which stands on git mechanics alone and needs no empirical proof) as something that was witnessed.

AC2 -- git show 6954304 --stat: three files changed -- docs/agents/protocols/GIT_MERGE.md (+7/-3), docs/issues/ISS-0210.yaml (+6/-3), and this run's own handoffs/WF03-ISS0210-20260821/step-03-git-merge-push-gap.json (+9/-9, this run's bookkeeping, not new attested content). No re-opening of the force-with-lease rule text, the union-driver decision, or the ORCHESTRATOR.md pointer sentence -- ORCHESTRATOR.md does not appear in this commit at all, and the diff hunks in GIT_MERGE.md and ISS-0210.yaml touch only the two flagged sentences (plus the mechanical line-wrap of the following unchanged sentence in ISS-0210.yaml's YAML block-scalar, not a content change).

Separately, on the top-level status bookkeeping note: agree the reasoning is sound. ORCH's dispatch text mistakenly repeating the claim-step instruction into a rework note is ORCH's own dispatch-text error, and correcting a mechanical bookkeeping field (top-level status) after result.status was already correctly PASS is not new attested content requiring a rework round-trip. This is a MINOR against ORCH's dispatch-authoring, not a reason to FAIL this run.

VERDICT: PASS on both AC1 and AC2. No outstanding issues from this narrow re-gate.
